subject: english
question:
Find the part of the given sentence that has an error in it. If there is no error, choose ‘No error’.

Dr. Stone returned to the UK at January 2001 to begin data analysis.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 3)**

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **primary issue** in the sentence is the use of the preposition** "at"** instead of** "in"** before "January 2001."
 
• **When referring to months and years, the correct preposition is *"in."***
 
• The correct phrase should be ***"in January 2001,"*** ensuring **grammatical correctness and clarity.**

Therefore, the correct statement is** *"Dr. Stone returned to the UK in January 2001 __to begin data analysis."***

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **A: "Dr. Stone returned to," **– This part of the sentence is** grammatically correct **and does not require any changes.
 
• **B: "to begin data analysis."** – This part of the sentence is **grammatically correct** and does not require any changes.
 
• **D: "No error"** – This would be the correct option if there were no mistakes in the sentence, but there is an error in part C.
